annotations.actionTaken: Cast Winternight Stories without first making a land drop, despite having Swamp and Restless Reef in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (untapped) first, then cast Winternight Stories using the other 3 lands, leaving the new Swamp untapped for potential plays after drawing 3 cards.

annotations.description: Winternight Stories allows discarding just one creature card instead of two non-creature cards. Discarding two Swamps (net +1 card) instead of one Harvester of Misery (net +2 cards) costs an extra card. While Harvester is powerful, with 3 lands on board plus Restless Reef, Gloomlake Verge, and Watery Grave still in hand, the second Swamp is nearly worthless - making the effective cost of keeping Harvester very low.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded 2 Swamps to keep Harvester of Misery, netting only +1 card from Winternight Stories.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Harvester of Misery as the creature card to satisfy Winternight Stories with only 1 discard, netting +2 cards. Harvester won't be castable for 2+ turns, and the extra Swamp kept is low-value given the abundance of lands already available.

annotations.description: Opus Valley targeted Greasewrench Goblin with Bitter Triumph instead of Marauding Mako. The Goblin's exhaust ability was already used (evidenced by the +1/+1 counter), making it just a 3/2 body. Marauding Mako grows with every discard trigger, and o3 Tinker is running a discard-synergy deck with Bloodthorn Flail in hand, Inti in graveyard (recurring discard value), and the overall deck strategy centered on discarding cards. The Mako would become a much larger threat over time.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to destroy Greasewrench Goblin (a 3/2 with no remaining abilities) with Bitter Triumph
annotations.betterLine: Destroy Marauding Mako, which scales with every discard and poses a much greater long-term threat in this discard-synergy deck

annotations.description: Missed lethal. Could have discarded Flamewake Phoenix to equip Bloodthorn Flail onto Bloodghast (equip cost: discard a card), triggering Monument to Endurance for 'each opponent loses 3 life' (opponent goes from 6 to 3), then attacked with a 4/2 Bloodghast for exactly lethal (3 + 4 = 7 > 6).
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with an unequipped 2/1 Bloodghast for only 2 damage, putting opponent to 4 life.
annotations.betterLine: In main phase, discard Flamewake Phoenix to equip Bloodthorn Flail to Bloodghast. Monument to Endurance triggers - choose 'each opponent loses 3 life' (opponent to 3). Then attack with 4/2 Bloodghast for lethal.

annotations.description: Exiling Winternight Stories (which has Harmonize - castable from graveyard) and Archenemy's Charm (a powerful removal/recursion spell) for evidence when there are clearly expendable cards available. Stock Up (3) + Bitter Triumph (2) + Intimidation Tactics (1) = 6 MV exactly, all with no graveyard utility.
annotations.actionTaken: Planned to exile Archenemy's Charm and Winternight Stories for evidence 6
annotations.betterLine: Exile Stock Up (3) + Bitter Triumph (2) + Intimidation Tactics (1) for evidence 6, preserving Winternight Stories (Harmonize from graveyard) and Archenemy's Charm for potential recursion

annotations.description: Opus Valley is at 2 life and chose only the tutor mode of Insatiable Avarice (pay {2} to search), which just puts a card on top of their library. They need an answer RIGHT NOW to survive - Flamewake Phoenix is already attacking them. By not also choosing the draw-3 mode (+{B}{B} to draw three cards and lose 3 life), they could have... wait, they're at 2 life, so paying 3 life would kill them. The tutor-only mode means they won't draw the card until next turn's draw step, and they need to survive this turn. However, given they're at 2 life, the draw mode would be suicide (lose 3 life at 2 HP). So the tutor mode is actually the only viable choice. But the real question is whether casting Insatiable Avarice at all is correct here - they have all lands tapped and 3 Requiting Hex in hand. Looking more carefully: all their lands are tapped, so they already cast the Insatiable Avarice. The tutor-only mode is the only one that doesn't kill them. This seems reasonable given the constraints.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose tutor mode only for Insatiable Avarice
annotations.betterLine: Actually, this was the only viable choice since drawing 3 and losing 3 life at 2 HP would be lethal
